expected_level_description: You can: - manage service components to ensure they meet business needs and key performance indicators (KPIs)
You can: - work under guidance to identify process optimisation opportunities - contribute to the implementation of proposed solutions
You can: - design solutions and services with security controls included, specifically engineered to mitigate security threats
You can: - identify and apply modern development standards to support complex projects and programmes - lead others in applying modern development standards

You can: - collaborate with others when necessary to review specifications - use the agreed specifications to design, code, test and document programs or scripts of medium-to-high complexity, using the right standards and tools

You can: - approach prototyping as a team activity, actively soliciting prototypes and testing with others - establish design patterns and iterate them - use a variety of prototyping methods and choose the most appropriate
You can: - identify, locate and fix complex service faults - advise others on different methodologies and types of service support

You can: - design systems characterised by medium levels of risk, impact, and business or technical complexity - select appropriate design standards, methods and tools, and ensure they are applied effectively - review the systems designs of others to ensure the selection of appropriate technology, efficient use of resources and integration of multiple systems and technology

You can: - establish standards and procedures across a service product life cycle, including the development product life cycle, and can ensure that practitioners adhere to these - manage resources to ensure that the systems integration function works effectively

You can: - collaborate with user researchers and can represent users internally - explain the difference between user needs and the desires of the user - champion user research to focus on all users - prioritise and define approaches to understand the user story, guiding others in doing so - offer recommendations on the best tools and methods to use

You can: - analyse how a service fits into care pathways across organisations - work with clinicians, care staff, and patients to shape digital services - explain the effect of digital decisions on care, safety, and staff workload
You can: - take part in hazard workshops and contribute to a hazard log - follow the clinical risk management process for your work - provide evidence for a clinical safety case, such as test results

You can: - lead data protection impact assessments and information sharing agreements - advise teams on lawful basis, consent, confidentiality, and retention - investigate incidents and recommend improvements
You can: - prioritise vulnerabilities by risk, including to patient services - scope and manage penetration tests and remediation
You can: - monitor alerts and triage them using runbooks - gather evidence and escalate events - tune simple detection rules under guidance
You can: - line manage a team, setting objectives and running appraisals - support wellbeing and manage attendance, performance, and conduct - plan the team's development and succession
You can: - track spending against a small budget and raise variances - authorise spending within your limit
